frames.narration: Alice and Bob have the document open, and the text is 'CAT'. Both connected through a gateway, and the router sent both to the same document server, which owns this document.
At the same instant, Alice types X at the start and Bob deletes the final T. Each sees their own change at once, without waiting for the server: Alice has 'XCAT' and Bob has 'CA'.
Both operations travel to the gateway, based on version 12. They are sent to the document server in the same instant.

The server puts them in order: Alice's first. It is accepted as version 13. Bob's operation was written for version 12, so it is transformed against Alice's insert: 'delete at 2' becomes 'delete at 3', since a letter was added in front.

states.doc: v13: XCAT, then Bob's op becomes delete at 3

frames.narration: Both operations are appended to the log before anything is acknowledged, so a crash now would lose nothing.

The server tells each person what they missed. Alice gets Bob's delete at 3 and applies it to 'XCAT', giving 'XCA'. Bob gets Alice's insert and applies it to 'CA', giving 'XCA'. Everyone's text is now identical.
Meanwhile Bob's cursor moves. Cursor positions go on a separate presence channel: throttled, never stored, and shown to Alice as a coloured marker.
After a few hundred operations the document server saves a snapshot of the text. Opening the document later means loading the snapshot and replaying a handful of operations.
